sqe:position-deletes:v2.notes: MoR DELETE on a V2 table without identifier fields writes position-delete files (PositionDeleteFileWriter) and commits a RowDelta; data files are not rewritten. The tests pin 'format-version' = '2'. Spark 4.1 with Iceberg 1.12 reads an SQE-written position delete back and returns the same rows.

sqe:equality-deletes:v2.notes: On a table with identifier fields, merge-on-read DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE write equality-delete files (EqualityDeleteFileWriter) and commit one RowDelta; no data file is rewritten. The tests assert added-equality-delete-files in the snapshot summary, then read the table from Spark 4.1 with Iceberg 1.12 and require the same rows as SQE. SQE declares identifier fields with ALTER TABLE ... SET | DROP IDENTIFIER FIELDS; identifier_fields_set_drop_switch_update_mode asserts that SET turns a copy-on-write UPDATE into an equality delete and DROP turns it back.

sqe:equality-deletes:v3.notes: Same as V2 on a V3 table: keyed merge-on-read DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE write equality-delete files in one RowDelta (summary asserts added-equality-delete-files), and Spark 4.1 with Iceberg 1.12 reads the same rows as SQE.

sqe:merge-on-read:v2.notes: DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE route through RowDeltaAction when write.*.mode = merge-on-read. With identifier fields, UPDATE writes a data file plus an equality delete for the old keys, and MERGE composes MATCHED UPDATE, MATCHED DELETE and NOT MATCHED INSERT into one RowDelta. Without identifier fields UPDATE and MERGE fall back to copy-on-write and DELETE writes position deletes. Each Spark interop test asserts the merge-on-read summary before Spark reads the table back.
caveats: UPDATE and MERGE are merge-on-read only on tables with identifier fields (ALTER TABLE ... SET IDENTIFIER FIELDS); without them they fall back to copy-on-write.

sqe:merge-on-read:v3.notes: MoR DELETE on a V3 table writes deletion vectors (never position-delete files); with identifier fields DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE write equality deletes in one RowDelta. Spark 4.1 with Iceberg 1.12 reads each result back with the same rows as SQE.
caveats: UPDATE and MERGE are merge-on-read only on tables with identifier fields (ALTER TABLE ... SET IDENTIFIER FIELDS); without them they fall back to copy-on-write.

sqe:copy-on-write:v2.notes: DELETE / UPDATE / MERGE in copy-on-write mode (the default) rewrite the affected files through ReplaceFilesAction.

sqe:copy-on-write:v3.notes: DELETE on a V3 table without a declared MoR property runs CoW: rewrites the matched files via RewriteFilesAction, drops the row from subsequent SELECTs, and commits a fresh snapshot through Polaris.

sqe:schema-evolution:v3.notes: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT on a V3 table commits write_default and initial_default; rows written before the ALTER read the initial default (#830) in projections and predicates, new rows that omit the column get the write default (#828).

sqe:type-promotion:v2.notes: ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE accepts int->long, float->double and decimal precision widening, refuses every other change before commit, and reads files written before the promotion as the new type (#859).

sqe:type-promotion:v3.notes: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE widens columns on V3 tables (int -> bigint, real -> double, decimal precision widening, unknown -> any primitive; other changes are refused before commit, #859). The new type surfaces through information_schema.columns and the schema change commits through Polaris.
caveats: Nanosecond-to-microsecond narrowing not attempted (Iceberg spec rejects narrowing).
date -> timestamp (a V3 promotion) is refused: the reader path for it is untested.
A list element or map value cannot be promoted; struct members can (ALTER COLUMN s.a SET DATA TYPE).

sqe:column-default-values:v3.notes: CREATE TABLE ... DEFAULT <literal> and ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT set write_default and initial_default. INSERT with a column list and MERGE INSERT write an omitted column's write_default. Rows in files that predate the column read its initial_default, in projections and in predicates, on both coordinator scan paths and on workers. A quoted default on a DATE, TIMESTAMP, DECIMAL, BINARY or numeric column is stored as a value of the column's type (X'..' for bytes); binary, fixed and UUID defaults are written on INSERT and MERGE INSERT. Function-call defaults and values that do not parse as the column type are rejected with a clear error.

sqe:table-creation:v3.notes: CREATE TABLE is V3 when a column needs it (TIMESTAMP_NS, VARIANT, DEFAULT), when asked with WITH ('format-version' = '3') / TBLPROPERTIES, or by default_table_format_version. SQE forwards format-version as the reserved table property so REST catalogs create V3 metadata.

sqe:hidden-partitioning:v2.notes: CREATE TABLE ... PARTITIONED BY (...) accepts all six standard Iceberg transforms: identity (bare column), year/month/day/hour, bucket(N, col), truncate(L, col), and void(col). The clause is normalized from `PARTITIONED BY` to sqlparser's native `PARTITION BY` form by a pre-parser, then translated into an Iceberg UnboundPartitionSpec with explicit field IDs starting at 1000 (Polaris rejects null IDs). The writer uses TaskWriter + RecordBatchPartitionSplitter to compute partition values per row and route them to per-partition data files. Verified end-to-end against Polaris: identity, day, bucket, truncate, and 3-field composite specs all round-trip; INSERT + COUNT(*) + WHERE on the partition column return correct results.

sqe:hidden-partitioning:v3.notes: Same SQL syntax as V2 (PARTITIONED BY) and the same writer path. Verified on a V3 table with a TIMESTAMP_NS column partitioned by day(ts): INSERT routes per-row through the partition splitter and COUNT(*) returns the expected count.

sqe:partition-evolution:v2.notes: ALTER TABLE ADD/DROP/REPLACE PARTITION FIELD evolves the partition spec end-to-end. Pre-parser in sqe-sql/partition_evolution.rs lifts the non-standard syntax into a PartitionEvolution AST. The coordinator's apply_partition_evolution handler builds a new UnboundPartitionSpec from the current default spec, assigns continuing field ids from metadata.last_partition_id() + 1, and commits TableUpdate::AddSpec + SetDefaultSpec { spec_id: -1 } via the REST table-commit endpoint. Read path was already correct (per-file partition_spec_id from iceberg-rust). Writer was patched so the unpartitioned fast path stamps the current default spec_id when spec_id != 0.

sqe:partition-evolution:v3.notes: V3 metadata stores per-file partition_spec_id the same way V2 does; the same coordinator handler and writer path exercise V3 nanosec timestamp partitioning unchanged.

sqe:multi-arg-transforms:v3.notes: PARTITIONED BY accepts only single-source transforms; a multi-source transform cannot be declared.

sqe:time-travel:v2.notes: FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF + 6 metadata TVFs (Step 8c).

sqe:time-travel:v3.notes: FOR VERSION AS OF works end-to-end on V3 tables: the classifier strips the clause, apply_version_spec registers a snapshot-pinned provider under datafusion.public.<alias>, and the SQL is rewritten to reference it. SELECT against the pinned snapshot returns the historical row count.

sqe:table-maintenance:v2.notes: All four CALL system.* procedures ship with both parser unit tests and live e2e tests that go through docker-compose.test.yml (Polaris + RustFS): `rewrite_data_files_returns_summary` plus `rewrite_data_files_actually_compacts_parquet`, `expire_snapshots_retain_last_commits`, `remove_orphan_files_respects_default_threshold`, `rewrite_manifests_commits_and_returns_summary`. The new compaction strong-form test inserts ten separate data files via ten INSERT statements, runs `CALL system.rewrite_data_files(min_input_files => 5, target_file_size_bytes => 1073741824)`, and asserts: input_count > output_count in the summary row, SELECT COUNT(*) preserved, table_files TVF shows fewer live files than before. rewrite_data_files does real Parquet re-encoding via `rewrite_group` -> `read_parquet_file` + `write_data_files`, with row-count invariant checked before commit and post-commit metadata-cache invalidation. Earlier matrix caveats describing it as manifest-only were stale; the real re-encoding shipped in MR !96 and the row-count invariant + commit safety in MR !98.

sqe:table-maintenance:v3.notes: CALL system.rewrite_data_files merges files on V3 tables with real Parquet re-encoding; row count preserved, file count drops, snapshot log moves forward. Same maintenance code path as V2: `rewrite_group` reads input data files via the table's FileIO, accumulates RecordBatches, and writes new Parquet files through the same `write_data_files` helper that powers INSERT and CTAS. Format-version 1/2/3 ride the same code path because re-encoding operates on Arrow batches, not on Iceberg metadata. expire_snapshots / remove_orphan_files / rewrite_manifests also work against V3 metadata. Verified by `rewrite_data_files_on_v3_table` (V3-specific) plus the strong-form `rewrite_data_files_actually_compacts_parquet` (10 small files -> fewer files, row count preserved, table_files TVF reports smaller live count).

sqe:branching-tagging:v2.notes: ALTER TABLE CREATE/DROP BRANCH and TAG with retention options, SET WRITE_BRANCH routes INSERT / DELETE / UPDATE to a branch, FOR VERSION AS OF '<ref>' reads it.

sqe:branching-tagging:v3.notes: Same transaction actions apply to V3 tables: on a format-version 3 table, SET WRITE_BRANCH routes INSERT / DELETE / UPDATE to a branch and FOR VERSION AS OF '<ref>' reads it.

sqe:read-support:v3.notes: SELECT against V3 tables works through the existing iceberg-rust scan path: TIMESTAMP_NS columns materialise as Arrow Timestamp(Nanosecond), INSERT/SELECT round-trips, COUNT(*) and projections all return the expected results.

caveats: Geometry writes are not supported (separate cell).

sqe:write-merge-update-delete:v3.notes: DELETE (CoW, and MoR via deletion vectors), UPDATE (CoW and MoR equality) and MERGE INTO commit on V3 tables; each path has a V3 e2e test.

sqe:bloom-filters:v2.notes: Every data-file write path builds WriterProperties through build_writer_props, which emits Parquet bloom filters; the footer test re-reads the file and finds the bloom offset. DataFusion uses them at scan time. Puffin carries NDV sketches, not blooms. The Iceberg spec keys write.parquet.bloom-filter-enabled.column.<col> / -fpp.column.<col> are honoured too: an SQE INSERT into a table Spark configured writes blooms for exactly those columns, struct members included.
caveats: write.parquet.bloom-filter-max-bytes is ignored: parquet-rs sizes a filter from the row count. Members of lists and maps get no bloom.

caveats: write.parquet.bloom-filter-max-bytes is ignored: parquet-rs sizes a filter from the row count. Members of lists and maps get no bloom.

Path (2) verified by list_namespaces_via_glue_rest in the same test file, listing namespaces and tables in a pre-existing S3 Tables bucket through SigV4-signed REST. Phase O+ step 2 closed the engine-wiring gap on path (1): `SessionCatalog::for_session` dispatches on `[catalog].backend` so a coordinator configured with `[catalog.backend] type=glue` routes SQL through the GlueCatalog. sqe:variant-type:v3.notes: VARIANT columns (and JSON columns on V3 tables) store Iceberg variant, unshredded. JSON text is parsed on write (invalid JSON fails the write), values read back as JSON text, CTAS / INSERT SELECT keep the type, the json_* functions accept a variant, variant_get / try_variant_get read typed fields from the binary encoding (Spark semantics), and rewrite_data_files keeps every value. Verified on the local Polaris stack, on the worker path, and across engines with Spark 4.1 + Iceberg 1.12 in both directions (Spark reads an SQE table after a merge-on-read DELETE; SQE reads a Spark-written VARIANT table).

sqe:shredded-variant:v3.notes: SQE reads and writes shredded variant files. Read: Spark 4.1 + Iceberg 1.12 writes a table with write.parquet.shred-variants=true (the test asserts typed_value is in the parquet schema), and SQE folds typed_value back into the variant on the coordinator's direct read, on the iceberg-rust reader and on a worker. Variant manifest bounds are skipped rather than parsed as primitives. Write: with write.parquet.shred-variants=true SQE infers a shredding per data file from its first batch (object fields of one primitive type, nested objects, or a whole-value primitive) and writes typed_value; rows that do not fit are written to the residual value unchanged. The test asserts typed_value in every file's footer, Spark 4.1 + Iceberg 1.12 reads the same JSON and typed field values as SQE, and rewrite_data_files keeps the shredding. Objects, arrays, extra keys and NULLs read back as the same JSON text.
caveats: Shredded columns are unshredded on read, so typed_value gives no pruning or typed field access.
Only top-level variant columns are shredded on write; a variant nested in a struct, list or map is written unshredded.

sqe:geometry-type:v3.notes: No GEOMETRY / GEOGRAPHY type in SQE DDL or the read path.

sqe:nanosecond-timestamps:v3.notes: TIMESTAMP_NS(N) / TIMESTAMPTZ_NS(N) map to Iceberg timestamp_ns / timestamptz_ns and to Arrow nanosecond timestamps; CREATE, INSERT and SELECT round-trip through Polaris.

sqe:unknown-type:v3.notes: Top-level unknown columns work across engines. SQE declares one as UNKNOWN or VOID, reads a Spark-written VOID column as NULLs, inserts around it and promotes it with ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE, and Spark 4.1 + Iceberg 1.12 reads every stage. Unknown columns and unknown struct members (also in a list of structs) are never written to a data file, as the spec requires; readers fill them with NULLs. Spark-written nested unknown members read in SQE, and Spark reads SQE's. A list of unknown, a map with an unknown value and a struct whose members are all unknown can be declared and read by both engines; neither SQE nor Iceberg Java can write a row (Parquet has no column for them), and the test asserts both refuse. ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE checks the spec's promotion rules, so unknown promotes to any primitive type and a narrowing is refused before commit. Iceberg Java 1.12 refuses unknown -> int in Spark, so SQE is the engine that promotes here. A nested unknown member is promoted with ALTER COLUMN s.u SET DATA TYPE; Spark reads the promoted table. information_schema.columns reports an unknown column as unknown, as DESCRIBE and the Trino endpoint do.

sqe:lineage:v3.notes: Row lineage is maintained at write time on V3 tables: new rows inherit fresh _row_id from first-row-id at commit; CoW DELETE / UPDATE / MERGE, MoR UPDATE / MERGE and rewrite_data_files carry _row_id and _last_updated_sequence_number into the files they write. Updated rows keep _row_id and get a newer sequence number; untouched rows keep both values; inserted rows get unique new ids. The merge-on-read UPDATE and MERGE cases run on a keyed table and assert added-equality-delete-files; Spark 4.1 with Iceberg 1.12 then reads the same _row_id and _last_updated_sequence_number as SQE.
caveats: MoR DELETE is not a lineage case (deleted rows have no successor).

sqe:deletion-vectors:v3.notes: MoR DELETE on a V3 table writes one Puffin deletion vector per data file, merges the file's existing deletes into it and retires the superseded vector in the same RowDelta. The test asserts added-dvs / removed-dvs in the snapshot summary, no added-position-delete-files, and the visible rows. Spark 4.1 with Iceberg 1.12 reads the table after both DELETEs and returns the same rows.
